Oyo offers traffic advisory ahead Olubadan coronation

The Oyo State Government has announced a temporary closure of key roads in Ibadan ahead of the coronation of Oba Rashidi Ladoja, as the 44th Olubadan.

The affected routes will be closed from 7:00 am on Friday, September 26 for smooth movement and tight security as dignitaries, including President Bola Tinubu, are expected to attend.

According to the organising committee, vehicles will not be allowed through Beere Junction inward Mapo Hall, Born Photo Junction inward Oja’ba, Idi-Arere Junction inward Oja’ba, and Itamerin Junction inward Mapo Hall.

Source: X | Oyo State Government
----

For more stories: https://t.co/YMxNq6Frsl

NEWS UPDATE: The Office of Student Regent (OSR) has issued Memorandum No. OSR-RDLC 2025-001 urging all student councils and students to participate in the Systemwide Day of Action for Higher University of the Philippines (UP) Budget on Sept. 25, coinciding with the national budget deliberations for state universities and colleges (SUCs)

Following UP’s largest budget cut in the decade amounting to Php 2.08-billion for fiscal year 2025, the proposed Php 46.85-billion budget for FY 2026 is set to suffer a Php 21-billion deficit under the National Expenditure Program.

In line with GASC Resolution No. 2025-017, which pushes for a stronger campaign for higher budget for the state subsidy, the OSR enjoined all the nation’s scholars to stage protest actions and different forms of mobilization to press demand for sufficient funding.

🇨🇳🇹🇼 DEADLY SUPER STORM SLAMS CHINA AFTER LEAVING 15 DEAD IN TAIWAN

Nearly 2 million people have been evacuated in southern China as one of the year’s strongest storms batters Hong Kong, Macao, Shenzhen, and Guangzhou.

In Taiwan, a dam collapse triggered catastrophic flooding, killing at least 15 and leaving 17 missing.

The storm had earlier torn through the Philippines and is now shutting down major Asian cities.

Source: CNN

DUTERTE’S ICC RECKONING: THE BLOOD-SOAKED MIRROR RUTO CAN’T ESCAPE

In a long-overdue smackdown for despots, former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte who turned his “war on drugs” into a slaughterhouse of extrajudicial carnage – has finally been slapped with three counts of crimes against humanity at the @IntlCrimCourt today. 

We’re talking his direct hand in the cold-blooded murders of at least 76 innocents, from Davao street sweeps to presidential hit squads mowing down “high-value targets” and low-level users like they were vermin, all part of a genocidal purge that tallied up to 30,000 bodies by human rights tallies. 

Locked up in The Hague since March 2025, this 80 year-old thug is now staring down a trial that could bury him for good, proving even the most swaggering tyrants get their day in the dock. 

But here’s the gut-punch truth they don’t want you swallowing: Duterte’s depraved playbook is the spitting image of that genocidal baboon and bottomless thief William Ruto’s vicious 2024-2025 rampage against Kenya’s soul. 

Remember the tear-gas chokeholds on Gen Z streets, the live rounds ripping through peaceful protesters chanting for tax relief, the midnight abductions of dissenters who dared whisper against the Finance Bill’s fiscal rape? 

Or how about the ghosting of bloggers and authors, the brave keyboard warriors exposing corruption vanishing into police cells, tortured into silence or worse? 

It’s the same script: a “crackdown” on imagined threats that masks a war on the poor, with cops playing judge, jury, and executioner, racking up dozens dead and thousands brutalized under the guise of “order.” 

Don’t kid yourself – this isn’t coincidence; it’s a flashing red alert from The Hague that Ruto’s indictment train is chugging right behind, maybe months out if the ICC’s Philippines probe sets the precedent. 

That Hague hammer drops on kleptocrats who drown democracy in blood and ballots, and Ruto’s ledger; bloated with stolen hustler funds and protest graves – is screaming for scrutiny. 

While Duterte rots in custody, Kenya’s ape-in-chief better enjoy his fleeting throne; the world’s watching and justice has a long memory for monsters like him.
